title: stage → apply → delete is not transactional and has no failure-path cleanup, so PII-bearing scratch rows leak
what_is_wrong: `stageRows`, `applyBatch` and `prisma.importStaging.deleteMany` are three independent commits with no transaction and no `try/finally`, so a throw anywhere after staging leaves the staging rows behind permanently, and a throw inside the upsert loop leaves the batch half-applied with no record of where it stopped.

title: `batchId` is built from a client-supplied header, so concurrent imports collide and silently drop rows
what_is_wrong: `requestId` is taken verbatim from the caller-controlled `x-request-id` header with no validation, and the batch key is a plain string concatenation of it with `orgId`, so the write surface of the key that partitions staged rows is nameable by the caller (R57's caller-nameable-key clause).

title: an empty or all-blank CSV crashes the handler with a 500
what_is_wrong: When the body is empty or contains only blank lines, `lines` is `[]`, `header` is `undefined`, and `splitLine(undefined)` dereferences `line.length` and throws a `TypeError` — the boundary never checks that a header row exists (RS3).

title: a missing or renamed `email` column silently rejects every row with no diagnostic
what_is_wrong: `indexOf` returns `-1` for an absent column and `f[-1] ?? ""` yields an empty string, so the required `email` column being spelled `e-mail` or missing produces rows with empty emails that `applyBatch` then counts as `rejected` — an unsatisfiable header is reported as bad data.

title: the size limit is applied after the whole body is buffered, and counts UTF-16 code units rather than bytes
what_is_wrong: `await req.text()` materialises the entire request body in memory before any check, and `csv.length` counts UTF-16 code units, so a constant named `MAX_CSV_BYTES` does not bound bytes (RS3 — the defensive transform reads as a control while measuring the wrong quantity).

title: unbounded row count applied one sequential upsert at a time inside the request
what_is_wrong: Nothing caps the number of rows (5 MB of CSV is on the order of 100 000 rows) and each is a separate awaited round trip, while `stageRows` correctly chunks its writes at `CHUNK = 200` — the batching helper the same file already established is not applied here.
